text:
Nashville arrives at Pittsburgh on one day of rest after a 6-0 loss at Boston, where Michael DiPietro stopped all 28 shots. The Predators are 1-2-2 in their last five and have been outscored 19-11 in that stretch. Pittsburgh is 1-4-0 over the same span, but the Penguins just snapped a four-game winless run with a 4-0 win over Florida, with Arturs Silovs stopping all 26 shots. They're still without Bryan Rust and Ben Kindel. With Rust out, Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Crosby and Rakell, and Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte are playing more.

Our model has this close, at 3.10 expected goals for PIT and 2.98 for NSH (expected goals measure the quality of chances). At five on five, PIT has taken 53% of the expected goals in its games to NSH's 44%. On special teams, NSH's power play generates 0.62 expected goals a game to PIT's 0.47. In net, projected starters Juuse Saros (+1.5 goals saved above expected this season, -10.2 last) and Silovs (+1.0, -12.8 last) both rate better than a year ago.

Watch Steven Stamkos (35% to score) and Filip Forsberg (63% for a point) for Nashville, and Sidney Crosby (57% for a point) and Rickard Rakell, who is flagged as due, for Pittsburgh. Our under-the-radar pick is Nick Robertson, a fourth-liner with 2.5 expected goals over his last 10 games, at 20% to score.
